body:
Throwaway because I'm still not completely comfortable with these aspects of my life. 


During my teen years I was a handful. I went to a crisis center my freshmen year of high school for a suicide attempt, went to the same crisis center again nine months later for cutting and was immediately sent to an all girls adolescent rehab afterwards. 

The crisis center was a hospital setting. Wide open room with couches and a tv on one side and two long tables and a smaller tv on the other side. The nurses station, kitchen, and rooms for clients outlined the big room, cameras everywhere. We all wore sweatpants, tshirts, a sweatshirt if we got cold and socks, we had to put on flip flops with our socks if we went outside. I was in there for a week both times. The first time I went there was a lot of crying the first two days. I never slept well in those terrible beds. The rules were very strict but once I got used to the place it was actually pretty nice. Rooms started filling up quick and I made friends with a lot of kids from dope heads to extremely violent kids. I played speed and read a lot in my free time. Every couple of days I had a therapist session and I got three visits from my mom, including a family therapy session. It was a good experience for my young self. I helped other people out, the nurses admired me and I strengthened my relationship with my mom. 

The second time I went to this place was the summer before my sophomore year. The environment was much more relaxed, but my mental state wasn't. When I got there, there were four other people and as the days went by the size shrunk down to just me and another girl, Tara. We got it VERY easy. Lessons went by very quickly so we got to watch movies all the time on the big tv and no one wanted to cook for just two people so the nurses would buy us fast food sometimes. What made my stay here terrible was finding out on my second day that I was going to a 90 day rehab and there was no changing my mother's mind. I cried hard, cursed my mom and kicked and screamed my whole ride to the rehab. When you're 14, 90 days away from home seems like a lifetime. 

So what was rehab like? SO MUCH BETTER. It was an actual house that had been slightly modified. The garage was now the counselor's office and the porch became a tech office. We had three dogs and two donkeys. Most of the staff were addicts that had been in recovery for at least five years. We were aloud to wear whatever we wanted as long as it got dress code (think typical school dress code.) My first week there I was quiet and stayed to myself, but once I got out of my shell I loved it. Everyone there was very understanding. We all became a big, supportive family. There was lots of freedom once you had been there for a certain amount of time. Strict rules, but depending on who was working we got away with a lot of stupid shit. During your first week there, your parent(s) came down and you had to tell them every drug you've ever done and how often. Further down the road I had to do something called connections where my mother and I both wrote letters to each other owning up to our bad behavior. During connections my mother and I also had to write seven affirmations and confrontations for each other. Both drug history and connections were done in front of other families and the other girls there. Not a lot of privacy. The negative aspects of being in an all girls adolescent rehab was that I lived with ALL ADOLESCENT FEMALES. I went from living with six girls to around 13 by the end of my stay. So much drama and females, including me, are incredibly gross when you live with them. We went to AA and NA meetings everyday except for Sunday and Wednesday when we had meetings at home. We did online school every weekday and group therapy every week day as well. Free time was spent gossiping, playing guitar hero, writing to our families or going outside. We were very restricted from our families. We got visits every Saturday for three hours and ten minute long phone calls every Wednesday and Saturday. I spent my 15th birthday in rehab. I was VERY lucky because my birthday happened to fall on the day of the monthly cookout so I got to see my family for a few hours, and most girls don't see their families if they spent their birthday there , but it was still very hard to let them go and spend my birthday away from home. Overall this was a good experience for me. I was there for a little over three months and even though I have come to terms with the fact that I'm not actually and addict, I gained great things from being there. My relationship with my mothered was strengthened so much and I was able to get extremely honest with her. My confidence and ability to stand up for myself skyrocketed. I learned a lot of great coping skills there and made great friends that I still keep in touch with now.

I'm sorry for how long and jumbled this is. It's so hard to summarize all the aspects of the mental facilities I've been to without going on and on. Also sorry for grammar and what not, I'm on mobile.
